seo.title: Fix Wrong Information About Your Brand in ChatGPT
seo.meta_description: How to fix wrong information about your brand in ChatGPT and other AI tools: find the source, correct it everywhere, use feedback tools and monitor answers.

h1: How to Fix Wrong Information About Your Brand in ChatGPT and AI Answers
answer: To fix wrong information about your brand in ChatGPT and other AI tools, first find where the error comes from, usually an outdated listing, old article or inconsistent page. Correct it at the source and everywhere else your details appear, publish a clear page with the right facts, use each platform's feedback option, and recheck the answers over the following weeks.
key_takeaways: AI errors usually come from outdated or inconsistent sources.
Fix the source, not just the symptom.
Publish one clear, factual page about your business.
Use each platform's feedback tools on wrong answers.
Live-search answers update faster than training data.

sections.heading: Why AI tools get brands wrong
sections.body_html: AI assistants build answers from what they have learned and, for many questions, from live web searches. If an old directory lists your former address, an outdated article describes a service you no longer offer, or two of your own pages disagree on pricing, the AI may repeat the wrong version. Sometimes it combines facts from two businesses with similar names. Occasionally it simply produces an incorrect statement with no clear source.

sections.heading: Step 1: document the error
sections.body_html: Ask the question that produced the wrong answer in each major assistant, with web search on and off where possible. Record the exact wording, the date, the platform and any sources the answer cites. Cited sources are the most valuable clue: if the answer links to a page, that page is likely where the error comes from.

sections.heading: Step 2: find the source
sections.body_html:
1. Check cited links in the answer first.
  2. Search for the wrong fact in quotes to see where it appears online.
  3. Review your own site for old pages, PDFs or blog posts with outdated details.
  4. Check listings: Google Business Profile, Bing Places, directories, social profiles, review sites.
  5. Look for similar business names that could be confused with yours.

sections.heading: Step 3: correct it everywhere
sections.body_html: Update or remove outdated content on your own site, and redirect retired pages to current ones. Correct your business listings. Contact publishers of articles with factual errors and ask politely for a correction, giving the right facts and a source. For data that comes from directories, update each one; inconsistent listings are among the most common causes of wrong AI answers.

sections.heading: Step 4: publish the facts clearly
sections.body_html: Create or update an About or company facts page that states the essentials plainly: legal and trading name, founding date, location, services, leadership, contact details and anything commonly confused. Use the same wording everywhere. Add Organization structured data with your official name, logo and profiles. A clear, authoritative source makes it easier for AI tools to get the facts right.

sections.heading: Step 5: use platform feedback
sections.body_html: Most assistants let users rate answers or report problems, usually with a thumbs-down or feedback button on the response. Use it on the incorrect answer and explain the correct fact briefly. Google's knowledge panel help explains that verified entities can suggest edits to their own knowledge panels, which is worth doing if your business has one. Feedback alone rarely fixes an error, but combined with corrected sources it helps.

sections.heading: How long corrections take
sections.body_html: Answers based on live web search can change within days or weeks once the corrected pages are re-crawled. Answers based on a model's training data change only when the model is updated, which you do not control. That is why fixing sources and publishing clear, consistent facts matters: it improves live answers now and the training data of future models later.

sections.heading: When the problem is negative reviews or criticism
sections.body_html: If an AI answer reflects genuine criticism, the fix is not suppression. Address the underlying issue, respond professionally to reviews, and publish accurate information about what you have changed. Over time, newer reviews and coverage shift the picture. Never post fake reviews or pay for them; they violate platform rules and can make the problem far worse.

sections.heading: When the information is harmful or defamatory
sections.body_html: If an AI answer makes serious false claims that could harm your business, document everything carefully, report it through the platform's official channels, and consider getting legal advice. Most platforms have specific processes for reporting harmful or legally problematic content.

sections.heading: Preventing future errors
sections.body_html:
• Keep a master list of your official business facts.
  • Update every listing on the same day when something changes.
  • Redirect or update old pages instead of leaving them live.
  • Check key AI answers about your brand monthly.
  • Brief partners and directories when you rebrand, move or change services.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: An agency moved offices from Irvine to Anaheim, but ChatGPT still says it is in Irvine. The cited source is an old directory listing. The agency updates its Google Business Profile, Bing Places and the five directories that mention it, adds the new address to its About page and footer, updates Organization structured data, asks two local publications to correct old articles, and gives feedback on the wrong answer. A few weeks later, live-search answers show the new location.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Wrong AI answers almost always trace back to wrong or inconsistent information somewhere online. Find it, fix it everywhere, publish the correct facts clearly and recheck. Feedback buttons help a little; fixing the sources helps a lot.

faqs.q: Why does ChatGPT have wrong information about my business?
faqs.a: Usually because outdated or inconsistent information exists online, such as old listings, articles or pages on your own site, or because your business is confused with a similar name.

faqs.q: Can I contact OpenAI to correct my business information?
faqs.a: You can use the feedback option on the incorrect answer. The most effective fix is correcting the sources the AI reads and publishing clear, consistent facts.

faqs.q: How long does it take for AI answers to update?
faqs.a: Answers using live web search can update within days or weeks after corrected pages are re-crawled. Training data changes only when models are updated.

faqs.q: Does structured data help fix wrong AI information?
faqs.a: Organization structured data with your official name, logo and profiles helps machines identify your business correctly, alongside clear on-page facts.

faqs.q: What if the AI repeats negative reviews?
faqs.a: Address the underlying issues, respond professionally and let newer reviews and accurate information shift the picture. Never post fake reviews.

faqs.q: What if an AI answer is defamatory?
faqs.a: Document it, report it through the platform's official channels and consider legal advice for serious false claims.

faqs.q: How do I prevent wrong information in the future?
faqs.a: Keep a master list of business facts, update every listing at once when something changes, and check AI answers about your brand monthly.

faqs.q: Can I edit my Google knowledge panel?
faqs.a: Google's help explains that verified entities can suggest edits to their knowledge panels. Information is otherwise generated automatically from sources across the web.
